events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: The radio clicks on. Tuesday, February 2. Your clean shirt is folded exactly as the hotel left it. Record a voice memo nobody else can hear. It can be for Jo, for tomorrow's you, or for nobody at all. The small bottle of maple syrup is back on the dresser, wrapped and unopened. Choose what you physically do with it. The recorder is running. Before this Tuesday you remember 31 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.pack: Phil tucks the unopened maple syrup into his travel bag.
choices.leave: Phil leaves the wrapped bottle on the hotel dresser.
choices.open: Phil opens the bottle for himself this morning.
choices.pour_out: Phil empties the bottle into the hotel sink.

events.line: It’s in the bag. Eight o’clock, sharp, and I’m not leaving you to eat dry pancakes again.
events.effect: Phil tucks the unopened maple syrup into his travel bag.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: Rita and Larry wait at the cue sheet. Beside it is the only weather cartridge: your own cheerful voice doing an old forecast, down to a small breath before your first word. At seven, it can substitute for you on air. Do something with it while they can see. They can hear anything you say. Before this Tuesday you remember 31 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.pocket_cart: Phil pockets the station's only copy of his old weather recording.
choices.mark_archive: Phil writes ARCHIVE across the weather cartridge and leaves it by the cue sheet.
choices.leave_cart: Phil leaves the weather cartridge by the cue sheet, unmarked.

events.line: That is not an archive, it's my voice. Keep it.
events.effect: Phil pockets the station's only copy of his old weather recording.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: You just saw Phil at the cue sheet. Speak to him or to Larry, or let the moment go.

choices.tear_carbon: Rita gives Phil the yellow carbon copy of the cue sheet.
choices.keep_carbon: Rita clips the yellow carbon back under her sheet.

events.line: Phil, that's my carbon copy, not yours, but since the Rialto's closing after tonight, I'm giving you the whole damn thing so you can frame it. Don't even look at me like I'm trying to save you.
events.effect: Rita gives Phil the yellow carbon copy of the cue sheet.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: You're beside Rita. Phil can hear you. You can answer either one. The crew still has to get the equipment across the street.

choices.take_case: Larry picks up the equipment case.
choices.set_down: Larry sets the equipment case on the floor.

events.line: Hold on, if you touch that case I’m filing a formal complaint. Rita, you’re buying the coffee, this is a hostile takeover.
events.effect: Larry picks up the equipment case.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: The coach door is open. The projection booth across the street has a service door. There is a stairwell at the hotel where the radio can't be heard. Go where you actually want to go. You can speak under your breath. Before this Tuesday you remember 31 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.
events.line: Eight o'clock, sharp. I'm not fighting the static.

events.speaker: Alma
events.cue: The door is shut. Only Rita and Larry are with you. You have the key; the last reel has eight minutes left. They can bring a microphone, give you one private line to Nell, or pack up. You have not given permission. Open the conversation however you like.
events.line: Leave the phone. It’s not going to change what’s in Pittsburgh.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: Speak to Alma or Rita. They were not both at the hotel desk. You decide what to repeat, if anything. You have a pencil and an empty reel box.

choices.write_label: Larry turns the reel box over and writes on its blank label.

events.model_output: {"choice": "put_down", "line": "You're right. It's not going to change anything in Pittsburgh. But I'm still not touching that phone."}
events.line: You're right. It's not going to change anything in Pittsburgh. But I'm still not touching that phone.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: Alma and Larry are here with you. Their words are still in the room. There is exactly one line at seven. Ask for something you actually need, or refuse what's being asked.

choices.draw_chair: Rita pulls a chair over to Alma.
choices.stay_door: Rita stays by the closed door.

events.line: So the phone stays, and the projector keeps burning a hole in the curtain. Fine. I need the seven o'clock slot to run my own segment, and I'm not letting the boss keep stamping his name on my work.
events.effect: Rita pulls a chair over to Alma.

events.speaker: Alma
events.cue: Answer the people here. You can reserve your voice for Nell, let people hear it publicly as well, or withhold it altogether. Their jobs do not oblige you to help.

choices.family_only: Alma permits only a private call to Nell.
choices.public_too: Alma permits either the public microphone or a private call.

events.line: Seven o'clock is mine. Fix your own reel.
events.effect: Alma permits either the public microphone or a private call.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: One last thing you could say to either of them before the reel runs out.

choices.hold_door: Larry holds the door for Alma.

events.line: Rita, if you're gonna fix the reel, do it over here. Don't make me walk back to the desk.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: There is a telephone here. You can ring Jo in Pittsburgh, or let her have the afternoon to herself. If you call, say what she hears when she picks up. If you leave it alone, keep the line empty. Before this Tuesday you remember 31 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

events.speaker: Jo
events.cue: You are alone with the couch and the van booking. You haven't heard from Phil this afternoon. Say something out loud, or don't.

choices.fit_foot: Jo tries the couch foot again.

events.line: Come on, you stubborn piece of furniture. Phil's probably just reading the weather forecast to himself in the shed.
events.effect: Jo tries the couch foot again.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: A town phone directory gives the regional station's desk number. You can call Rita there, tape something for yourself or stay quiet. If you call, she picks up; your line is the only part heard at the other end. Before this Tuesday you remember 31 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.call_desk: Rita picks up the station telephone.
choices.memo: Phil keeps this recording to himself.

events.model_output: {"choice": "put_down", "line": "Eight o'clock, sharp. You know where the syrup is."}
events.line: Eight o'clock, sharp. You know where the syrup is.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: The phone is back on its cradle. Larry needs to know what to set up. Tell him what you want, or let him choose. He can still refuse.

choices.clear_space: Rita clears a space beside the patch.
choices.leave_space: Rita keeps her hands in her pockets.

events.line: Yeah, I'm doing this, so move your feet. Just load the tape and tell the boss it was an accident, because I'm not signing his name to my life.
events.effect: Rita clears a space beside the patch.

events.speaker: Larry
events.cue: You have time to prepare one input. Answer the people in this room. The old recording is usable only if it is here.

choices.set_mic: Larry tests the live microphone for Alma.

events.line: You want me to load it? Sure. I’ll just tell her it slipped out of the case, my bad.
events.effect: Larry tests the live microphone for Alma.

events.speaker: Rita
events.cue: Seven o'clock. Make the patch or let the slot go. Anything you say is to Larry and Alma inside the control room.

choices.silence: Rita lets the seven o’clock slot pass in silence.
choices.private: Rita patches a private call to Nell, who picks up. No voice goes on the air.
choices.public: Rita opens the public microphone. Alma’s words go out over the local station.

events.line: Don't test it, it's live. Put your name on the line, or don't.
events.effect: Rita opens the public microphone. Alma’s words go out over the local station.

events.speaker: Alma
events.cue: The microphone is live. Your voice is going over local AM. You cannot know who is listening.
events.line: It’s not an accident, Larry. It’s just a reel. Fix your hands, not the story.

events.speaker: Phil
events.cue: At seven you tuned to the regional frequency. What you heard: The AM radio carries Alma saying: It’s not an accident, Larry. It’s just a reel. Fix your hands, not the story. Now, hours later, the pocket recorder clicks on in your hand. Leave a private voice memo for morning about the part of today you can still hear. Speak as Phil, or play out the silence. Before this Tuesday you remember 31 complete days in this run ending before you could reach Wednesday breakfast.

choices.keep: Phil lets the last recording play to the end.
